published_source: Table 4, column 2 (Weight Loss), 'GLP-1 x months 1-6' row, from the JMR article text (data/text/jmr/00222437251412834.txt). Other bins: months 7-12: 0.0150 (0.0421); post-discontinuation: -0.0621 (0.0500). N = 60,428.
replication_status: failed (synthetic data by design; see notes)
notes: STATIC re-estimation of Table 4 column 2 (Weight Loss): treatment = household has adopted and is still using GLP-1 (months 1-12 of use); post-discontinuation months (the published 'month 1-6 (stopped)' bin) and months 13+ of continued use (which the authors drop as an unbinned NA) are excluded, so the sample is the authors' estimation rows minus the stopped bin. gvar g_idx = adoption month index (month 0, itself dropped); t_idx = consecutive month index 1-27 (month_num in the raw file skips 663). Household FE, month FE, clustered by household, no weights, no controls. Estimation sample follows the authors' Rmd: 2,602 adopters matched 1:1 (MatchIt nearest-neighbour logit, no replacement, on Jul-Dec 2022 covariates; match.csv re-created in the work dir because it is not shipped) to never-adopters; adoption month (month 0) dropped; the two months between last confirmed use and first confirmed non-use dropped; adopters' pre-period limited to months -6..-1; controls keep all 27 months (Jul 2022-Sep 2024). published_coef is the 'months 1-6' coefficient of the binned regression (Equation 1), the closest published comparator; it is not a static coefficient. Column sample = adopters in the subgroup (Weight Loss) plus their matched controls. SYNTHETIC DATA: the Dataverse package (doi:10.7910/DVN/SVWBNT) ships only Data_clean_synth; spending profiles are reshuffled across households and rescaled, so by design no coefficient reproduces (README Section 4). Adoption timing, use duration, discontinuation and stated reason are preserved (N and adopter counts for columns 1-3 match the paper exactly); income is not (synthetic 1,856/746 vs published 1,814/788 adopters).
